input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web
console. Cluster administrators can see, for each data science project, which
workbenches are sitting idle: each entry shows the workbench's last activity,
its owner, and its reserved resources. The report is sourced from the notebook
controller's existing activity tracking — no changes to the notebook controller
itself; its data is surfaced for the first time. The report also supports CSV
export so administrators can take the data elsewhere.

## Scope

- A new report surface in the web console, scoped per project, listing idle
  workbenches.
- Report columns: workbench name, last activity (from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking), owner, and reserved resources (the workbench's resource
  reservations and attached storage).
- Data sourcing from the notebook controller's activity tracking; the mechanism
  by which the console reads that data (e.g. from the workbench's status or
  another readable source) is an implementation decision for the Dashboard team.
- Idle classification based on last-activity age; the specific idle threshold
  used for the report is an implementation decision.
- CSV export of the workbench report, including the displayed rows and columns.
- Empty-state handling for projects with no idle workbenches.
- No reclamation, deletion, or other mutating actions on workbenches from the
  report (automated reclamation is out of scope for the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with varying recent activity, the
  report lists each idle workbench with its last-activity time, owner, and
  reserved resources.
- Given a project with no idle workbenches, the report shows an empty state
  rather than an error.
- The last-activity values shown in the report match the notebook controller's
  activity tracking for the same workbenches (validation of the Notebooks
  component as a passive data source).
- An administrator can export the workbench report as CSV, and the exported
  file contains the rows and columns displayed in the console.
- The report offers no action that stops, deletes, or otherwise mutates a
  workbench — reporting only.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking — fully covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of this report is included here rather than
  a separate epic — the export edits the same report surface this epic builds,
  so splitting would double-touch the same components.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the web console

## Description

This epic delivers a stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console. Cluster
administrators can see, for each data science project, completed pipeline runs
older than a configurable age that still retain artifacts, so they can identify
runs whose accumulated storage could be reclaimed. The report is sourced from
Kubeflow Pipelines' existing run completion metadata — no changes to Kubeflow
Pipelines itself. The report also supports CSV export.

## Scope

- A new report surface in the web console, scoped per project, listing stale
  pipeline runs.
- Report columns: run identity, completion time, age, and indication of
  retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- A configurable age threshold defining when a completed run counts as stale;
  the configuration mechanism follows existing console configuration patterns
  and is an implementation decision for the Dashboard team.
- CSV export of the pipeline-run report, including the displayed rows and
  columns.
- Empty-state handling for projects with no stale runs.
- No reclamation, deletion, or other mutating actions on runs or artifacts from
  the report (automated reclamation is out of scope for the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of varying ages, the
  report lists the runs older than the configured age, with their completion
  metadata and retained artifacts.
- The stale-age threshold is configurable, and changing it changes which runs
  the report lists.
- The run completion data shown in the report matches Kubeflow Pipelines run
  metadata for the same runs (validation of the Data Science Pipelines
  component as a passive data source).
- Given a project with no stale runs, the report shows an empty state rather
  than an error.
- An administrator can export the pipeline-run report as CSV, and the exported
  file contains the rows and columns displayed in the console.
- The report offers no action that deletes or otherwise mutates a run or its
  artifacts — reporting only.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run
  metadata — fully covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of this report is included here rather than
  a separate epic — the export edits the same report surface this epic builds,
  so splitting would double-touch the same components.

# Documentation for the idle resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation for the console's idle resource
reporting capability: what the idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run
report show, how to read and export them, and how administrators can safely
reclaim capacity based on what the reports surface. The documentation is
authored through the Red Hat docs content process once the reports are
implemented.

## Scope

Content outline (authored as new doc topics in the RHOAI documentation set):

- The idle-workbench report: what it shows (last activity, owner, reserved
  resources), where to find it per project, and how to interpret idle status.
- The stale pipeline-run report: what it shows (completed runs older than the
  configured age with retained artifacts), how the configurable age threshold
  works, and where to find it per project.
- Exporting either report as CSV and working with the exported data.
- Safe reclamation steps: how administrators can use the reports to reclaim
  capacity manually and confidently, including cautions about data that is
  still needed — while making clear the platform does not automatically
  reclaim or delete resources.
- Cross-references from the existing workbench and pipelines documentation to
  the new report topics where users would look for them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports — the idle-workbench report and
  the stale pipeline-run report — including their data columns and per-project
  scoping.
- Published documentation explains how to export each report as CSV.
- Published documentation explains safe reclamation steps and clearly states
  that no automated reclamation or deletion is performed by the platform.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports so
  that described columns, thresholds, and behavior match what ships.
- Documentation is delivered through the Red Hat docs content process.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps —
  fully covered by this epic. Substantive content authoring is a distinct work
  stream from the code implementation, which is why this is a separate
  docs-authoring epic rather than scope on the report epics.

  explicitly out of scope; report epics carry ACs that no reclamation/deletion
  actions are offered, so the reports cannot imply capability the platform does
  not provide.

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing; both data
sources are in-platform and generally available per architecture context.

No epic carries "RHOAI web console", "notebook controller", or "Kubeflow Pipelines" verbatim as its component. The decomposition summary goes further and makes the canonicalization explicit with a Component Graph mapping table (informal name → canonical name → active/passive classification → handling), which is exactly the right treatment for a strategy that uses informal names in its Affected Components section. Informal names do appear in epic *prose*, which is natural and harmless; the frontmatter `component` fields are what downstream Jira submission validates, and those are correct.

The bundling is defensible, not priority collapse: the export is an action on the very report surface each P1 epic constructs, so a standalone export epic would double-touch both surfaces and couldn't be scheduled independently. Priority inheritance is clean — E001/E002 are P1 matching their HLRs and block only the docs epic; E003 is P2 under the docs-authoring exception, and nothing blocks P0 work (nothing is P0).

**2. Epic boundaries — solid.** One component and one team per epic. Code implementation (E001/E002) and content authoring (E003) are correctly separated. Each epic is well under the ~2-week guideline. Each epic's CSV export covers only its own report, so no scope duplication.

Both edges into E003 are Rule 11 docs-authoring edges, correctly not treated as priority inheritance. E001 ∥ E002 parallelism is justified under Rule 15 with a concrete rationale. Critical path length 2 suits the strategy's size. No konflux/repo-onboarding chains exist, so those edge rules aren't implicated.

Scope fidelity — solid.** The epics decompose without designing: E001 explicitly defers the console's read mechanism for activity data ("status or another readable source... implementation decision"), E002 defers the threshold configuration mechanism to existing console patterns, and E001 defers the idle threshold (the strategy itself never defines "idle" for workbenches, so deferral is faithful, and the asymmetry with E002's configurable threshold mirrors the HLRs' actual wording).
